Dokis First Nation

Dokis First Nation’s relationship with the French River is a useful starting point for learning about its community-directed energy and land-management work. A community-approved case study and a detailed interview with its lands administrator document particular projects and their limits.

Read the sources [1] Indigenous Clean Energy / Indigenous Peoples Rights International / Business & Human Rights Resource Centre [2] Anishinabek News

01

Community decisions and a hydro partnership

The 2024 Okikendawt case study presents hydroelectric development as a long-term Dokis initiative involving community meetings, successive leaders and a partnership with Hydromega. Its methods explain that Dokis reviewed the account and held final approval. The report links the project with planning for community benefits. This supplies a community-approved perspective; it does not independently establish every financial or environmental outcome.

Read the sources [1] Indigenous Clean Energy / Indigenous Peoples Rights International / Business & Human Rights Resource Centre

02

Land administration and learning new technologies

In a 2025 interview, lands administrator Randy Restoule explains how Dokis uses drones and geographic information systems to obtain updated imagery and investigate changes along the French River. He also describes opportunities for young people to learn field and computer skills. These are his dated accounts of work and plans. The underlying measurements and individual property questions were not independently reviewed here.

Read the sources [2] Anishinabek News

The Dokis First Nation and the Okikendawt Hydro Power Project ↗

Publication: 2024-10

October 2024 case study, PDF pp.1–5 actually read: project background, methods, community involvement and decision making. Its methods state that Dokis held final edits and approvals. An affirmative project account, not an independent audit; financing records, underlying votes and environmental outcomes were not independently verified.

Inspection: Content reviewed for the stated scope

Scope: PDF pages1–5, selected complete sections1–7: executive summary, background, methods, project overview, community setting and decision-making.

Review recorded: October 27, 2026

Access note: Public actual-content body/PDF selected pages were read without a login. October2024 affirmative case study by project/Indigenous/rights partners. Methods state Dokis held final edits/approvals. Underlying votes, finance, agreements, trust records and environmental audit not independently inspected. No sensitive practices or sites reproduced.
